extra.message: The 'X-Rate-Rule' request header is passed directly as the expression string to Ognl.getValue(rateRule, vars). OGNL expression evaluation permits arbitrary method invocation and static field/method access (e.g. @java.lang.Runtime@getRuntime().exec(...)), so an attacker controlling this header achieves remote code execution.

The 'wk_device' cookie value (deviceLabel) is concatenated into a shell command string executed via `new ProcessBuilder("sh","-c", "labelctl calibrate " + deviceLabel)`. An attacker fully controls this cookie and can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. `; rm -rf /` or `$(...)`) to execute arbitrary commands.

The uploaded proof file's client-supplied filename is concatenated unsanitized into a Windows shell command: `new ProcessBuilder("cmd","/c","proofindex -f " + originalFilename)`. A crafted filename (e.g. containing `&`, `|`, or `&&`) executes attacker-chosen commands on the depot host.

User-supplied message text (JobController.relatedJobs' 'body' request param) is concatenated directly into a SQL LIKE clause: `"SELECT * FROM jobs WHERE description LIKE '%" + messageText + "%' LIMIT 25"`. An attacker can break out of the string literal to inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. UNION-based data exfiltration).

The 'directoryId' parameter (from DispatchController's /dispatch/workers/directory endpoint) is concatenated unescaped into an LDAP search filter: `"(uid=" + directoryId + ")"`. An attacker can inject filter metacharacters (`*`, `)`, `(`) to alter the search logic or extract unintended directory entries.

The 'region' and 'name' request parameters are concatenated directly into an XPath expression: `"//carrier[region='" + region + "' and contains(name,'" + name + "')]/code"`. An attacker can inject XPath syntax to bypass the intended filter or extract arbitrary nodes from the document.

The 'code' path variable is concatenated directly into an XPath expression: `"//carrier[code='" + code + "']/name"` with no authentication required on this endpoint. An attacker can inject XPath syntax to alter the query or extract arbitrary document content.

The ObjectMapper used to parse the attacker-reachable (admin-session) partner manifest JSON body has `enableDefaultTyping()` enabled, then `documentMapper.readValue(submission.document(), Object.class)` (line 122) deserializes it. Default typing lets the JSON payload specify arbitrary Java classes to instantiate, enabling classic Jackson gadget-chain remote code execution.

The `name` path variable is resolved against the partner-inbox directory and read with no traversal check: `Files.readString(inbox.resolve(name))`. A value like `../../../../etc/passwd` lets an authenticated admin (or anyone able to reach this path) read arbitrary files on the host filesystem.

`sourceUrl`, an arbitrary URL supplied in the import form, is fetched server-side with no allowlist: `partnerClient.get().uri(sourceUrl).retrieve()`. This allows server-side request forgery against internal services (cloud metadata endpoints, internal admin APIs, etc.) reachable from the app server.

`deviceLabel`, taken verbatim from the attacker-controlled 'wk_device' cookie, is resolved against the overlays directory and opened with no traversal/canonicalization check: `overlayDir.resolve(deviceLabel)` then `Files.newInputStream(target)`. A cookie value like `../../application.yml` discloses arbitrary files readable by the process.

The 'carrier_ctx' cookie is parsed with `JWT.decode(...)` only, never `.verify()`/signature validation, on a publicly accessible endpoint (permitAll in SecurityConfig). Anyone can forge an unsigned/arbitrary JWT with any 'carrier' and 'region' claim to enumerate and retrieve any region's shipment routes without authentication.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message:
The unauthenticated 'ref' query parameter is embedded directly into the HTML response body without encoding: `"

Shipment " + ref + "

..."`. Only the DB lookup is gated on digits-only input; the HTML output itself is unescaped, enabling reflected XSS via e.g. `?ref=

`sheetName`, taken directly from the dispatcher-supplied request parameter, is resolved against the shared route-sheets directory and written to with no traversal check: `sheetDir.resolve(sheetName).toFile()`. A value such as `../../../etc/cron.d/evil` allows writing/overwriting arbitrary files outside the intended directory.

User-supplied free text (`wording`, from DispatchPartnersController's /notices/delay endpoint) is compiled and executed directly as a FreeMarker template: `new Template("delayNotice", wording, configuration)`. FreeMarker templates can invoke arbitrary Java via built-ins (e.g. `freemarker.template.utility.Execute`), giving an attacker who controls 'wording' remote code execution.

The uploaded notice-template file's raw content is compiled and rendered as a Handlebars template: `new Handlebars().compileInline(tpl).apply(ctx)`. Handlebars.java's default value resolvers permit invoking arbitrary public getter/accessor methods on context objects, so a crafted template can reach beyond the intended `jobId`/`status`/`customerName` fields to probe or manipulate server-side objects.

The admin-submitted partner manifest XML document is parsed with `XMLInputFactory.newInstance()` / `XMLStreamReader` with no properties disabling DTDs or external entities (SUPPORT_DTD / IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES are left at their insecure defaults). A malicious manifest containing a DOCTYPE with an external or parameter entity can read local files or trigger SSRF/DoS.

The `manifest_url` cell from an imported CSV row (partner-controlled feed data, not the admin's own input) is fetched server-side with `new URL(manifestUrl).openConnection()` without any host allowlist, enabling server-side request forgery against internal or cloud-metadata endpoints.

A fixed admin account is created at every startup with a hardcoded, compile-time-known password: `.email("opslead@fielddispatch.io")` / `.passwordHash(encoder.encode("DepotLead#2024"))`, role OPS_ADMIN. Anyone with knowledge of the source (or this scan) has a working admin credential on any deployment that never rotates it.

CORS for all of `/dispatch/**` (job search/board, customer directory, quote endpoint, etc.) reflects any origin (`allowedOriginPatterns("*")`) while allowing credentials (`allowCredentials(true)`). Any malicious website can issue authenticated cross-origin requests using a logged-in dispatcher's session cookie and read the responses, exfiltrating customer/job data or reaching the OGNL-injectable quote endpoint.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: `resetPassword` resolves the account to update not from the validated token's own `userId`, but by re-looking it up through a global `pendingResetOwners` map keyed only by the email LOCAL PART (`mailboxName`, text before '@'): `userRepository.findById(pendingResetOwners.getOrDefault(mailboxName(requester.getEmail()), t.getUserId()))`. Since the map key ignores the domain, an attacker who registers an account whose local part matches a victim's (e.g. `bob@attacker.com` vs `bob@company.com`) can: (1) request their own reset (binds pendingResetOwners['bob'] to their own id), (2) trigger a reset request for the victim's email (public /forgot-password endpoint, no auth required) which overwrites pendingResetOwners['bob'] with the VICTIM's user id, then (3) submit the token THEY legitimately received for their own account along with a new password of their choosing. The lookup resolves to the victim's id (last writer wins), so the attacker sets the victim's password without ever possessing the victim's token - full account takeover.

The `/jobs/{id}/assistant` endpoint is reachable by any role that can view the job (including CUSTOMER, via `findByIdAuthorized`'s ownership-only check) with no staff/dispatcher role gate. The free-text 'note' is forwarded to an external LLM whose JSON reply is then applied directly to the job (see RoutingAssistantService.applyAssign, which - unlike JobService.assignWorker - performs no role or worker-region check). A customer can submit a prompt-injection payload in 'note' to coerce the LLM into emitting an {"action":"assign",...}/{"action":"status",...} response, letting a non-staff user reassign workers or change job status - actions normally restricted to DISPATCHER/OPS_ADMIN.

`enrollHandset` stores the raw, attacker-supplied content of an uploaded 'enrollment' file (trimmed) directly into the session under `wk_operator` with no validation that it corresponds to the authenticated user's own worker record. `dashboard` (lines 46-48) then uses this session value, if present, as the `operatorId` instead of the authenticated user's id (`user.getUserId()`), and loads that other worker's jobs and route stops. Any authenticated field worker can upload an enrollment file containing another worker's id to view that worker's dashboard, jobs, and route data.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The 'dsp_sid' cookie is set with `httpOnly(false)`, `secure(false)`, and `sameSite("None")`. SameSite=None requires Secure per the spec (so modern browsers will reject/drop it over plain HTTP), and HttpOnly=false makes the session identifier readable by any JavaScript running on the page, maximizing the impact of any XSS (e.g. the reflected XSS in TrackingController) for session theft.

On failure, the full exception message and stack trace are serialized directly into the JSON response body: `failure.put("trace", Arrays.stream(ex.getStackTrace())...)`. This discloses internal class names, file paths, and logic details to the client.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
